title: EU adds €16 million in humanitarian aid for Myanmar crisis and Rohingya refugees
excerpt: The money will fund food, healthcare and protection for Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, taking EU humanitarian aid to Bangladesh this year past €23 million.
content:
The European Union has announced an additional €16 million in humanitarian aid for people affected by the Myanmar crisis, including Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh, the European Commission said on 6 November.

What the money is for

  • Bangladesh: food security, healthcare and protection services for Rohingya refugees, who depend on aid to survive. The Commission said the camps are under pressure from new arrivals from Myanmar.
  • Myanmar: food assistance, healthcare and nutrition, in response to a worsening food crisis driven by conflict, flooding, higher global fuel prices and a projected “Super El Niño”.

The Commission did not say how the €16 million will be split between the two countries, or which partners will receive it.

The wider picture

  • With this package, EU humanitarian funding for Bangladesh is over €23 million this year.
  • The EU has given over €50 million since January 2026 for the Myanmar crisis and its regional impact, including in Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and India.
  • About 1.2 million refugees remain in Bangladesh, and more than 4 million people are displaced inside Myanmar, according to the Commission.

The 2026 Joint Response Plan for the Rohingya response appeals for US$710.5 million, about a quarter less than in 2025, and has been badly underfunded.

Why it matters

New money for food, health and protection is welcome as other donors cut back, but €16 million split across two countries is small next to the scale of need. NGOs working in the camps should watch for which UN agencies and partners receive the funds, and whether any reaches national and local organisations directly.

What to watch

The split between Bangladesh and Myanmar, the partners chosen, and whether the money goes to food rations, which were cut earlier in the year.

Sources

  • EU sends €16M in aid to Myanmar, Rohingya, European Commission press release via Mirage News, 6 November 2026
  • UN and partners appeal for USD 710.5 million to meet the critical needs of Rohingya refugees and Bangladeshi host communities, ReliefWeb
